title: Chapter 5: The sluice
licence: Original sample written for this project
text: Beyond the gate there was no light except the glow of old roots in the ceiling. The torn map ended there, and Ines did not know which of the three passages led to the upper sluice. Pim remembered that Sabela had said the trees always leaned toward clean water. He pointed out that the glowing roots in the left passage were bright, while the others were dull and crusted. They followed the bright roots upward for most of an hour. The water grew louder and the air grew warmer. The passage ended at a wooden sluice wheel that held back a black pool of snowmelt. The wheel had not turned in many years, and the two of them could not move it. Ines braced the coil of rope around a spoke and a rock pillar and twisted it tight with the handle of Pim's knife. The wheel gave a quarter turn and stopped. Then Tomas arrived, soaked and bleeding from the forehead. He said the carters had fled up the stair, and that he had left Sabela resting by the gate. He took hold of the wheel beside them without asking to be forgiven. With the three of them pulling, the sluice opened. Snowmelt poured down the channel and swept the salt out of the spring. The roots above their heads brightened one after another. Ines asked Tomas whether he would tell the village what he had carried down the stair. Tomas answered that selling the field had been his choice, but that he would not be the man who let the orchard die, and he agreed to speak.
